title: Latency Timewarp: cohort breakout and IO-mode segmentation by model & route
creator: Priya Patel
description: Build a new latency dashboard and underlying telemetry plumbing called "Latency Timewarp" that lets SREs and platform engineers slice p50/p95/p99 by model and route with a streaming vs non-streaming (IO-mode) toggle, and cohort playback by request shape. This ticket covers: (1) trace hook additions to propagate servepath metadata (route, model, io_mode, kv_cache_hit, batch_size), (2) metric and log pipeline updates to include canonical IO-mode labels, and (3) a dashboard UX with percentile heatmap, timeline timewarp scrubbing, and comparison mode for two time windows. The goal is to reduce MTTI for performance regressions and enable rapid root-cause for streaming/non-streaming regressions across models.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing spans emitted from runtime include servepath tags: route, model_name, io_mode (streaming|sync), batch_size, kv_cache_hit
Prometheus/metrics or ClickHouse tables can be queried to produce p50/p95/p99 by model + route + io_mode for arbitrary time windows
Dashboard implements: percentile heatmap, timewarp scrubber, compare-two-windows mode, and links to example traces
Streaming vs non-streaming toggle properly filters traces/metrics and preserves percentile calculations
Alerts adjusted or documented: new p95/p99 SLO breakouts for model-route IO-mode where customer_impact==high
End-to-end test: synthetic job generates streaming and sync requests and dashboard reflects expected separation
Docs and runbook updated with queries, dashboard links, and troubleshooting playbook
technical_notes: Instrumentation: runtime (Go) will add tags to top-level servepath span via TraceHook: 'route', 'model', 'io_mode', 'batch_size', 'kv_cache_hit'
Language SDKs (python/node) should propagate a request-level header 'x-rw-servepath' for downstream correlation where available
Metrics: introduce 'response_latency_ms' histogram with histogram_buckets tuned to 1ms..30s; store aggregates by (model, route, io_mode)
Logs: add structured fields 'servepath.model','servepath.route','servepath.io_mode' for Loki/ES ingestion
Backend storage: ClickHouse table 'latency_servepath_v2' will get new partition keys for (model, route, io_mode); use materialized views for p50/p95/p99
Trace sampling: ensure sample rate for high-traffic routes >= 1% and increase to 5% when p99 deviation alert triggers
Dashboard: Grafana panel for percentile heatmap + custom React panel for timewarp scrubber linking to Trace Explorer

Design (Owen Brooks): make the timewarp scrubber keyboard-navigable and add playback speed control

risks_and_tradeoffs: Adding io_mode as a dimension increases cardinality — mitigated by storing raw events in ClickHouse and only exposing aggregated labels in Prometheus
Higher trace sampling rates increase cost; we will use adaptive sampling tied to percentile anomalies
Materialized views need careful TTL to avoid storage blowup — propose 30d hot window, 1y cold aggregates
UI complexity: too many toggles can confuse users; prioritize a small set of common comparisons and keep advanced filters hidden
implementation_plan: 1) Runtime change: add TraceHook and emit servepath tags (ENG runtime team) - PR #1789
2) Telemetry pipeline: update collector to map 'servepath.io_mode' to ClickHouse column and avoid Prometheus explosion

5) Test: synthetic generator job to produce mixed streaming/sync workload and validate metrics
6) Rollout: enable on staging, monitor overhead, then rollout gradually to prod routes with high customer_impact
7) Runbook: publish troubleshooting steps and alert playbook
